analysis: What changed vs Friday's 9 AM brief: the tape went from bad to historic, then flipped overnight. Friday's close was far worse than the 9 AM read — S&P -3.70% to 6,910.39 (not -1.5%), Nasdaq -5.28%, Dow -1.93%, VIX closing at 35.89 (+26.2%), with both the S&P and Dow now confirmed in correction, more than 10% below record highs, after a seventh straight down day and the worst week since 2020 (S&P -8.6%, Nasdaq ~-10%). The overnight reversal is sharp but explicitly fragile: futures strengthened through the morning (S&P +2.24% at 2:29 AM ET to +2.9% by ~4:21 AM ET) and every Mag 7 name is green premarket, led by Nvidia +8.6% on Trump's Sunday Truth Social push to rehire Jensen Huang and Bessent softening on Meet the Press — but the board already ruled out reinstatement last week, and Monday's NYT report that US intelligence believed Alice Huang was in contact with a Chinese MSS officer from spring 2025 adds a fresh overhang the bounce is ignoring for now. The CrowdStrike-Zscaler deal ($43.9B all-stock, confirmed Monday) is the one genuinely new, company-specific catalyst and a sign M&A is still moving through the drawdown. Anthropic holding ~$92, comfortably above the $83 IPO price, takes the 'IPO as top' pressure off the tape for a day, though the FT's greenshoe criticism keeps the debate alive. Signal vs noise: the correction confirmation, the VIX closing above 35, the breadth of Friday's selloff (healthcare -6.2%, industrials -7.4%, discretionary -6.9% — not just tech), and gold's Friday bounce to $3,612 are signal; the premarket snapback is the open question — Capital Economics calls it 'mechanical' and a 'dead cat bounce', Swissquote says the AI 'bubble has burst', while Saxo notes a rebound doesn't require the problems to be solved. Community signal was thin overnight: HN threads on the Nvidia/Anthropic stories are low-engagement and add nothing beyond the headlines, and no qualifying Reddit thread surfaced. The week ahead is data-heavy into a holiday-shortened tape: PMI today, HPE/Agilent/Zoom earnings, then Wednesday's PCE/GDP dump before Thanksgiving. The test into the open is whether the bounce holds once cash trading starts, and whether the VIX gets back below 30.

headlines.headline: Futures rebound sharply after the worst week since 2020: S&P 500 futures +2.9%, Nasdaq 100 +3.8%, Dow +2.0% premarket (as of ~4:21 AM ET, stockanalysis). The bounce strengthened through the morning from +2.24%/+3.02% at 2:29 AM ET (Reuters). All three indexes closed last week in correction after Friday's rout.
headlines.why_it_matters: A sharp snapback after a historic down week — but analysts are split on whether it is a durable turn or a mechanical bounce, so the open matters more than the futures print.

headlines.headline: Nvidia (NVDA) +8% premarket to ~$135.76 after closing Friday at $125.53, down 14% (Morningstar/Barron's). President Trump posted Sunday on Truth Social urging the board to rehire Jensen Huang ('the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.'), and Treasury Secretary Bessent softened his stance on Meet the Press. The board said last week it does not intend to reinstate Huang, with Colette Kress as interim CEO and Heidrick & Struggles running the search. The NYT reported Monday that US intelligence believed Alice Huang was in touch with a Chinese MSS officer from spring 2025 until fall 2026; Huang is due to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month.
headlines.why_it_matters: Political pressure for Huang's return is the freshest Nvidia catalyst, but the board has already said no — so the pop is sentiment and short-covering fuel as much as substance, and the new NYT report adds fresh overhang. Record Q3 (EPS $2.68 vs $2.47 expected, revenue $115.84B, Q4 guide ~$130B) is not what the stock is trading on.

headlines.headline: CrowdStrike (CRWD) agreed Monday to buy Zscaler (ZS) in an all-stock deal valuing Zscaler at about $43.9 billion — 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share, ~$260.41, a 34% premium to Friday's close. Zscaler +13.4% premarket; CrowdStrike -5% (Reuters). The deal follows Friday's Bloomberg report of talks, after which Zscaler jumped ~17% after hours.
headlines.why_it_matters: The biggest cybersecurity deal ever, confirmed rather than rumored — M&A is still moving through the drawdown, and the premium validates Zscaler's Friday after-hours spike.

headlines.headline: Broad megacap rebound premarket (CNBC board): Meta +8.6%, Amazon +7.3%, Tesla +6.9%, Apple +6.7%, Microsoft +4.9%, Alphabet +4.5%, plus Broadcom +7.8%, Oracle +7.4% and CoreWeave +7.8%. Anthropic (ANT) ~$91-92, +3.5% premarket, holding above its $83 IPO price after closing Friday at $88.91 (-8.5%); CNBC notes an FT piece questioning whether bookrunners should have exercised the greenshoe.
headlines.why_it_matters: The whole AI complex is bouncing together, not just Nvidia — a risk-on reset after a week when even Friday's green names were only defensives.

headlines.headline: Friday's close was far worse than the morning read: S&P 500 -3.70% to 6,910.39, Nasdaq -5.28% to 22,617.73, Dow -1.93% (CNBC/dailymarket.report). Seventh straight S&P loss, longest streak since Feb 2020; S&P -8.6% and Nasdaq ~-10% on the week. The VIX closed at 35.89, +26.2% on the day. S&P and Dow both confirmed corrections, more than 10% below record closing highs (Reuters).
headlines.why_it_matters: The context the bounce is reacting against: a genuine correction with a 35+ VIX, so even a 3% futures pop leaves the tape fragile and headline-driven.

headlines.headline: Rates and havens: 10-year Treasury ~4.96%, up ~5 bps as money rotates back to risk (Morningstar); 2-year ~4.70% (+7.6 bps), 30-year ~5.335%. Gold ~$3,619 (+2.95%) after closing Friday at $3,612.30 (+2.76%); WTI ~$82.10 (-1.6%); Bitcoin ~$61,371 (+1.2%) after dipping below $60,000 Friday for the first time since July. December Fed hike pricing still near-certain (~92-96%).
headlines.why_it_matters: Yields ticking back up with equities is the risk-on half of the bounce; gold holding its Friday gains shows haven demand has not fully unwound.
